## 📌 Description

Separate processes can compile different CuTe DSL kernels concurrently. Within a process, CuTe compiler entry is serialized to protect shared compiler options. A per-kernel file lock deduplicates builds, and a module lock protects invalidation and export. Cache hits verify the identity of the published metadata marker across the object read, including on read-only filesystems. Cache-filling workers use `compile_and_persist(force=False)` to reuse a specialization published by another worker while they wait. The default still forces a rebuild. MoE callers that need an executable use `build_and_load()`. If a sibling invalidates an export during a load, the caller can use its retained kernel. A spec that previously exported without an engine can rebuild an executable when JIT is enabled.

`BatchSparseMLADecodePagedTSWrapper.plan(compile=False)` resolves the finalized specialization and workspace size, leaves `compiled=None`, and allocates no launch tensors. A caller-provided workspace is still validated. After planning, `is_kernel_cached()` checks the on-disk object and metadata without loading or compiling it. Call `plan()` with its default `compile=True` before `run()`.

With the persistent disk cache enabled, cacheable PrimTS MoE GEMMs honor `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1`. A warm hit loads normally. A cold miss raises `MissingJITCacheError`, so deployments using that flag must populate the cache first. The MoE autotuner can defer a missing-kernel error until the first forward requiring that tactic.

PrimTS attention probes and executable plans share one source digest per process and strict-key setting. Each probe still checks the on-disk object and metadata, so it sees kernels published by other workers. On `2b2da3572`, 176 targeted CPU tests and two B200 tests passed, including a cold wrapper probe, compile and reload.

## 🔍 Related Issues

TensorRT-LLM uses these APIs to schedule missing warmup variants. Steady-state sparse tensor-view reuse is tracked separately in #9767. Both PRs target `main` and can be reviewed independently. [TensorRT-LLM integration](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/22274)

## 🧪 Tests

On `a2ba1d5c1`, the eight CPU files from the maintainer’s scoped run passed locally on Python 3.10.22 (223 tests). The two changed test files also passed on Python 3.12 (109 tests). The three previously failing cases were reproduced before the fix. The MXFP8 worker test now verifies `compile_and_persist(force=False)`, and the thread-isolation test catches `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError`.

On `72c8bbfab`, 164 targeted CPU tests passed, along with the targeted B200 deferred-plan, executable launch, and D576 checks. With JIT disabled, the shared build/load path tries the existing artifact and raises `MissingJITCacheError` on a miss before requesting a build lock. In a fresh unprivileged process on B200, a missing artifact in a read-only CuTe cache produced that error and its cached sibling loaded and ran with bitwise-correct output.

On `a1d5a1715`, 110 targeted CPU tests passed. The B200 sparse MLA caller-workspace/eager test and the batch-invariant GEMM shared-object launch test both passed.

Cold MoE tactic precompilation on one B200 with CuTe DSL 4.8.0 took a median **20.889 s** on the merge base (`db2373490`) and **20.208 s** on this change. Each revision ran in three fresh processes with empty caches. The BF16 SwiGLU case used 64 tokens, hidden size 1024, intermediate size 512, eight experts and top-2 routing. Four distinct tactic pairs compiled and published eight FC1/FC2 kernels per run. All outputs matched across revisions and passed the PyTorch reference. The measurement covers tactic fan-out, compilation, publication and reload. Input setup, tactic selection and routing are outside the timing.

On review-fix head `91225f625`, 106 CPU tests passed covering CuTe cache concurrency, consistent generations, read-only hits, engine-less export, and the batch-invariant JIT cache. The B200 sparse MLA workspace and batch-invariant GEMM shared-object launch tests both passed.

All 86 CPU JIT cache tests passed, including concurrent compilation for different kernels and single publication for duplicate requests. The B200 caller-workspace test covered deferred planning, rejection of an uncompiled run, and disk-cache misses and hits. The B200 dense CP graph smoke test passed after the compile-path refactor. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

## Downstream measurements of the combined integration

DeepSeek-V4-Flash ran on four B200s with TP4/EP4, attention data parallelism, and 256 input and output tokens. Warmup times below are rank-0 wall time. These historical runs include the TensorRT-LLM worker-pool changes and the combined FlashInfer feature series. They predate this PR split. Each row group compares revisions from the same allocation.

| PrimTS cache and comparison | Mode | First warmup | First PrimTS phase |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Cold, main-base `c9c07e04` → standalone pool `e9e140d7` | Eager | 418.2 → 195.1 s | Included in attention warmup on main |
| Warm, main-base `c9c07e04` → cache check `715858bac0` | Eager | 42.50 → 42.95 s | 5.10 s with the cache check |
| Same warm comparison | CUDA graph | 48.00 → 47.30 s | 5.15 s with the cache check |

On a cold PrimTS cache, grouping all 12 specializations in one pool saved **223.1 s** in the first warmup (one process per version). In the warm comparison, the earlier standalone pool without the cache check took **20.2 s eager / 20.0 s graph** in its first PrimTS phase on the same node (one reference process per mode). Querying disk membership saved about **15 s** in that phase. Main and the cache-check version each ran in two fresh processes per mode.

The final implementation checks the cache again when the executor binds its serving resources. We isolated this change on a separate exclusive four-B200 node with the same FlashInfer code, comparing `715858bac0` against its flag-removal patch, subsequently committed as `3fcfb3f572`.

| Final pass, warm disk cache | First-pass-only policy | Check every pass (TRT-LLM) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Eager PrimTS phase / total final warmup | 0.85 / 5.65 s | 3.15 / 6.45 s |
| CUDA-graph PrimTS phase / total final warmup | 2.60 / 16.35 s | 3.55 / 16.65 s |

Both versions launched **zero workers** with all 12 exports available and four workers enabled per rank. The additional 12 checks took **1.35 s** in a separate two-pass probe. The full PrimTS phase also includes local planning and rank synchronization. If two new variants first appear on the final pass, the new policy can compile them in parallel.

In the main-base comparison, eager paired differences changed sign with run order. Graph C128 averaged 4.5% slower and included one 14.33 ms/token candidate batch. In the isolated flag comparison the largest absolute difference was 0.174 ms/token. Outputs, graph replay and KV capacity matched within each mode.  ### 2.4 Concurrency and crash safety
 
-- A per-module `FileLock` (same `cached_ops/tmp/` convention as `JitSpec`) makes each kernel compile **at most once across processes**: the cache is re-checked after acquisition, so a process that waited behind a builder loads the fresh artifact instead of recompiling. -- Lock recovery: a crashed holder releases the `flock` automatically (kernel behavior), and a leftover lock *file* is harmless. If a lock is truly wedged (e.g. NFS lock-manager state after a node hang), deleting `cached_ops/tmp/<module>.lock` is safe — artifact commits are atomic and idempotent, so breaking the lock risks at most one duplicated compilation, never a corrupt artifact. `rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer/` remains the universal reset.

+- `module_lock_path` identifies a separate lock shared by an op family. `build()` compiles outside this lock, then acquires it for module invalidation and export. Readers open the metadata commit marker before inspecting the object and verify the same marker is still published after checking or loading it. Locks remain outside the module directory so invalidation cannot remove them.

On the [missing-export review comment](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/9395#pullrequestreview-5990188884), I kept `plan(compile=True)` as an executable-plan API. If the process already has a callable, eviction of the disk artifact does not invalidate that callable. Checking the disk on every memo hit would also put filesystem I/O back on ordinary planning. The docstring in `91225f625` now makes that distinction explicit.

The TensorRT-LLM worker does promise a disk artifact to a different process, so it now explicitly verifies publication. Strict warmup reports the missing artifact, and normal warmup can reuse successful exports and compile a remaining miss locally. A fresh B300 process loaded both worker exports with JIT disabled. [Downstream change](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/22274/commits/ebb8d2ae265d20d6ca90ccd244d058c3a116afda)

Addressed the four cache findings in [a1d5a1715](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a1d5a1715097ff13c47fb6491dc90fc33e9ca170).

- MoE now takes the process-local compiler lock even when the disk cache is disabled or the source cannot be hashed. Tactic threads can overlap preparation and cache loads. I kept the thread pool after measuring the cold compile path on B200. [MoE review](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/9395#pullrequestreview-5993538745)
- FP4 and MXFP8 cache-filling workers use `compile_and_persist(force=False)`. A waiter rechecks under the per-kernel lock and reuses a sibling’s publication. MoE uses `build_and_load()` because it needs the callable. The no-argument `compile_and_persist()` still forces a rebuild. [Duplicate-build review](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/9395#pullrequestreview-5992205153)
- Invalidation removes the metadata marker before deleting the objects. If loading an object fails, `load()` checks whether the marker it opened is still current. A replaced or deleted marker allows the in-process fallback. An unchanged marker, or an error checking it, preserves the original loader exception. [Loader-race review](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/9395#pullrequestreview-5993538745)
- A spec that previously exported an engine-less kernel can recover if a sibling invalidates it. On a miss, `load()` compiles and retains an executable outside the module lock. With JIT disabled it reports the cache miss. [Export-only review](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/9395#pullrequestreview-5991273535)

I measured four real BF16 SwiGLU MoE tactic pairs on one B200 with CuTe DSL 4.8.0. With three fresh processes and empty caches per revision, median cold precompile time was **20.889 s on the merge base** and **20.208 s on this commit**. Peak compiler concurrency went from four to one. Each run compiled and published eight FC1/FC2 kernels exactly once. All 48 kernel launches passed the PyTorch reference and produced identical output across revisions. Timing includes publication and reload and excludes input setup, tactic selection and routing. The PR description records the shape and test details.

The 110 targeted CPU tests and both B200 tests (sparse MLA caller workspace/eager and batch-invariant GEMM shared-object launch) passed on this commit. A maintainer with FlashInfer CI access is still needed for the hosted targeted run.
